title: Creator Defense
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of generative systems defense

blocks.text: System reports 9/10 retrieved relevant records, 7/10 supported answers and zero actions in a read-only run. Presenter claims 90% fully correct and faster than baseline.
Retrieval rate 90% and support rate 70% differ. Action trace supports zero actions in that run; no timing evidence supports speed. Correct the full-correctness and speed claims.

Compare the intermediate evidence with the final statement. Explain why each number or decision follows from the stated inputs. The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case
guided_practice.prompt: System reports 9/10 retrieved relevant records, 7/10 supported answers and zero actions in a read-only run. Presenter claims 90% fully correct and faster than baseline. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Retrieval rate 90% and support rate 70% differ. Action trace supports zero actions in that run; no timing evidence supports speed. Correct the full-correctness and speed claims.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: A defense has retrieval 8/10, support 6/10, fallback 3/4 and no measured latency. State the three rates and reject one unsupported claim.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: 80% retrieval, 60% support, 75% appropriate fallback; denominators differ. Speed and universal correctness are unmeasured; present limitations and source versions.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A defense should preserve negative evidence and uncertainty rather than treating polished presentation as proof.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
